message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has a rich set of physical, chemical, and nuclear properties. Below is a concise overview grouped by category:

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic & Nuclear** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Isotopes | Protium (^1H, 99.98 %), Deuterium (^2H, 0.02 %), Tritium (^3H, trace) |
| | Nuclear spin | ½ (protium), 1 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.7928 μ_N (protium) |
| | Half‑life (tritium) | 12.32 yr |
| **Physical (gas at STP)** | State | Diatomic gas (H₂) |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (at 0 °C, 1 atm) |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (121 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14 K) |
| | Specific heat (Cp) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 298 K) |
| | Thermal conductivity | 180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 300 K) |
| | Speed of sound | 1270 m s⁻¹ (at 20 °C) |
| | Refractive index | 1.000132 (at 589 nm, 20 °C) |
| **Chemical** | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride) |
| | Acidic strength | Strong acid when bonded to electronegative atoms (e.g., HCl, H₂SO₄) |
| | Basicity | Weak base as hydride (H⁻) |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Dipole moment (H₂) | 0 (non‑polar) |
| | Van der Waals radius | 120 pm |
| | Polarizability | 0.666 Å³ |
| | Hydrogen bonding | Forms weak H–H bonds; participates in H‑bonding with electronegative partners (e.g., water, alcohols) |
| **Reactivity** | Combustion | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Redox behavior | Acts as reducing agent (e.g., H₂ + metal oxides → metal + H₂O) |
| | Catalytic role | Used in catalytic hydrogenation, Fischer–Tropsch synthesis, ammonia synthesis (Haber process) |
| | Electrochemical | Standard hydrogen electrode (SHE) potential = 0 V vs. SHE |
| | Solubility | Low in water (~1.6 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C) |
| | Permeability | High permeability through many polymers (used in gas separation membranes) |
| **Applications** | Fuel | Hydrogen fuel cells (electrolytic, PEM, SOFC) |
| | Industry | Ammonia production, petroleum refining, metal processing |
| | Space | Rocket propellant (LH₂/LOX) |
| | Research | Cryogenic cooling, neutron sources (via tritium) |
| | Medical | MRI contrast agents (tritium labeling) |
| **Safety & Handling** | Flammability | Extremely flammable; flash point –59 °C |
| | Explosion limits | Lower: 4 % vol in air; Upper: 75 % vol in air |
| | Toxicity | Non‑toxic; inhalation can cause hypoxia due to displacement of oxygen |
| | Radioactivity | Tritium is radioactive (β‑emitter) |
| | Storage | Requires high‑pressure cylinders or cryogenic tanks; careful leak detection |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant element in the cosmos.
- **Diatomic gas**: Exists as H₂ under normal conditions; highly reactive and flammable.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Protium (stable), deuterium (stable, heavier), tritium (radioactive, used in nuclear fusion research).
- **Key role in chemistry**: Forms acids, bases, and covalent bonds; central to organic chemistry and biochemistry (e.g., water, carbohydrates).
- **Energy carrier**: Central to clean‑energy technologies (fuel cells, hydrogen economy) and industrial processes (ammonia, petroleum refining).

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
